plate_findings.evidence: thick, large, polygonal, dark-brown scales involving the trunk front

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 7 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G). A: Top-left panel labeled IV-23 shows abdomen with thick polygonal dark-brown scales, explicitly described in caption as XLI trunk front involvement. B: Top-middle panel labeled IV-21 shows lateral trunk with generalized dryness and dark brown scales described for XLI patients. C: Top-right panel labeled V-7 shows neck with dark ichthyotic scaling, a captioned site for XLI. D: Bottom first panel labeled V-9 front chest shows diffuse dark polygonal scales of trunk and limbs typical of XLI. E: Bottom second panel labeled V-9 back shows extensive fine to large scaling of back, captioned XLI trunk back site. F: Bottom third panel labeled V-9 arm shows arm with white to brown polygonal scales consistent with captioned XLI arm involvement. G: Bottom fourth panel labeled V-9 ear shows preauricular/ear scaling explicitly mentioned in caption and in-text for XLI.

in_text_mentions: In all the patients from the family, the most prominent features included generalized dryness and dark brown scales prominent on the skin (Fig. 2); in which trunk, ears, scalp and limbs were affected. In almost all patients the abdomen was more severely affected than the back and other parts of the body. Scales were confluent and lighter on the scalp. Face, palms and soles were not involved. The hair and nails were normal. Preauricular small scales were also observed in young individuals.
